title: Lesson 2: Cube Root by Magic — Vedic Units-Digit Inspection
learningGoals: Memorise the unique mapping: units digit of a perfect cube uniquely determines the units digit of its cube root.
Estimate the tens digit of a cube root by comparing the remaining digits to known cubes.
Find cube roots of 5-digit and 6-digit perfect cubes by Vedic inspection.
Distinguish cube root inspection from square root inspection.
coreIdeas: Unlike squares, cubes have a UNIQUE units digit mapping — each units digit maps to exactly one root units digit.
The tens (or hundreds) digit is found by estimating which consecutive integer cubes bracket the remaining digits.
This is a powerful board-exam technique — memorise the mapping and find cube roots of 6-digit numbers in under 15 seconds.

workedExamples.method: Units digit of 17576 is 6 → root ends in 6. Remaining digits (drop last 3): 17. 2³=8 ≤17< 27=3³. So tens digit is 2. Answer: 26.
Units digit 2 → root ends in 8. Remaining: 54. 3³=27≤54<64=4³. Tens digit 3. Answer: 38.
Units digit 8 → root ends in 2. Remaining: 373. 7³=343≤373<512=8³. Tens digit 7. Answer: 72.
Units digit 9 → root ends in 9. Remaining: 970. 9³=729≤970<1000=10³. Tens digit 9. Answer: 99.

starterPractice: Warm-up: What is the units digit of the cube root of a number ending in 3?
Guided: Find ∛9261 — start by identifying the units digit of the root.
Independent: Find ∛74088 using the two-step Vedic method.

microLessonPattern: Arya states the unique mapping property and shows the full table.
Student derives the mapping by cubing 1 through 9.
Student applies the units digit map to real perfect cubes.

Review challenges the student to state the mapping from memory.
